paragraphs.text: Reversing the decline in operating margin
Margin plan for the board meeting, February 2027
Harlow Fresh Markets
CEO, presenting to the board
Fictional company; synthetic figures from the briefing pack

slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
How can Harlow lift its operating margin from 1.0% to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost and with at least $20M of operating income in FY2026, and which actions should come first?
What caused the fall in operating margin since FY2023, and how large is the gap to close?
How much of the lost gross margin can promotions, private label and shrink win back?
Should Harlow cut store hours, and should it exit its weakest stores?
Does e-commerce make money, and how can Harlow keep delivery without draining the margin?
Which actions come first, and does the plan meet the target, the covenant and the capital limit?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO, asking the board to approve the margin plan

Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028; Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant); At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028; Delivery kept in some form; no closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote
Board meeting, February 2027
Closing the delivery service; New stores, acquisitions and refinancing; Sales growth from new formats

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix promotions, shrink and delivery pricing, not store hours, to get close to 3.0%
Gross margin and e-commerce, not wages, explain nearly four-fifths of the fall in operating income
–	Operating income fell from $47.9M to $15.3M while sales grew 6%
–	3.0% needs about $30M more a year; the FY2026 covenant needs $4.7M more
Fewer promotions, more private label and less shrink would win back about $17M of gross margin a year
–	38% of FY2025 promotional events lost money
–	Shrink is 3.1% of sales in the least-staffed stores, 2.3% in the best
Store hours should be moved, not cut, and the weakest stores exited as their leases end
–	An 8% hours cut could give back up to $10M of its $14.5M saving
–	Exiting the nine loss-making stores adds about $6.6M a year
E-commerce loses about $10M a year; the tested delivery fee cuts that by $2.8M and keeps the service
–	Each home delivery loses about $12, seven times a collected order
The plan gets to about 3.0% by FY2028 for $7.5M; its first two actions can clear the FY2026 covenant
–	Started at once, promotions and the fee lift FY2026 to about $23M
–	About $0.4M short of 3.0%; it also needs the 2027 wage rise absorbed
